# SOP-P1-L1-05 Planned shutdown - Hot Forge line

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-CN02, EQ-P1-L1-IH03  
Related: ECN-2026-003, MM-P1-L1-IH03, SOP-P1-L1-02

Purpose
1. Describe controlled sequence for planned shutdown of the Hot Forge line to protect personnel and equipment, preserve process setpoints and provide clear handoff for restart.

Scope
2. Applies to maintenance, operations and supervision responsible for EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-CN02 and EQ-P1-L1-IH03 during planned line outages.

Preconditions
3. Confirm planned outage has been authorized per ECN-2026-003.  
4. Verify maintenance work orders are issued and approved where required.  
5. Ensure affected production orders have been stopped and work-in-process is managed per SOP-P1-L1-02.  
6. Confirm maintenance reference MM-P1-L1-IH03 is available for induction heater specific procedures.

PPE
7. The following PPE is required for shutdown and maintenance activities: arc-rated clothing, face shield, dielectric gloves, hearing protection, safety footwear, and safety glasses. Site safety officer may add task-specific PPE per hazard assessment.

Critical values
8. The spindle warm-up time for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 21 minutes.  
9. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 72 L/min.

Procedure
10. Notify
10.1 Notify the production supervisor, maintenance planner and shift safety representative that the planned shutdown will commence. Reference ECN-2026-003 authorization code as applicable.  
Rationale: clear notification prevents unscheduled tooling damage and allows safe isolation.

11. Secure material
11.1 Remove or secure billets and fixtures from EQ-P1-L1-RR01 and EQ-P1-L1-CN02.  
11.2 Tag and isolate any tooling that will remain in place.  
Rationale: prevents entrapment or unintentional motion during energy isolation.

12. Control of hazardous energy
12.1 Isolate electrical feeds to EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-CN02 and EQ-P1-L1-IH03 using lockout-tagout processes in accordance with site policy.  
12.2 Verify zero energy at point of work with appropriate test instruments before proceeding.  
Rationale: ensures personnel safety during maintenance.

13. Induction heater checklist
13.1 Verify coil cooling water flow is at or above the minimum before de-energizing heated zones. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 72 L/min.  
13.2 If flow cannot be confirmed, delay de-energization until flow is restored or follow MM-P1-L1-IH03 contingency steps.  
Rationale: protect coil assembly and water-cooled components from thermal shock and damage.

14. CNC turning center actions
14.1 Initiate controlled spindle cooldown sequence on EQ-P1-L1-CN02 per manufacturer guidance. Observe the spindle warm-up time for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 21 minutes for thermal cycle planning; allow warm-up or cooldown as recommended when sequencing shutdown and restart to avoid bearing stress.  
14.2 Retract tooling and place the machine in a safe state for mechanical inspection and lubrication tasks.  
Rationale: maintaining spindle thermal integrity reduces bearing wear and runout risk.

15. Roll reducer and conveyor
15.1 Lock out drive systems on EQ-P1-L1-RR01. Inspect coupling guards and conveyor tracking before any mechanical work.  
Rationale: avoid mechanical collapse or pinch hazards.

16. Housekeeping and verification
16.1 Drain or secure fluids per maintenance instructions and collect waste in approved containers.  
16.2 Conduct visual inspection of electrical cabinets for moisture ingress, loose terminals, and evidence of overheating.  
Rationale: identify pre-failure indicators and ensure safe work environment.

Examples / scenario notes
17. Example: If scheduled bearing replacement on EQ-P1-L1-CN02 is planned, coordinate spindle cooldown to coincide with bearing prep and allow for the 21 minutes warm-up reference to plan pre-lubrication cycles. Use MM-P1-L1-IH03 only for induction-heater-related tasks.  
18. Example: If coil flow is below 72 L/min during shutdown prep, do not perform electrical isolation of heating elements; instead secure the heater in standby and escalate to maintenance planning.

Records to keep
19. Maintain the following records with the work order:
19.1 LOTO tags and verification test logs.  
19.2 Confirmation of coolant flow rate checks and instrument readouts when available. Record the statement: "The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 72 L/min." where applicable.  
19.3 Spindle thermally relevant notes referencing the warm-up guidance: "The spindle warm-up time for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 21 minutes."  
19.4 Photos of isolation points and component conditions.  
19.5 Completed maintenance checklists and sign-off forms.

Post-maintenance verification
20. Before re-energizing:
20.1 Confirm all guards and interlocks are reinstalled and tested.  
20.2 Validate coolant flow meets the stated minimum and is stable.  
20.3 Run equipment through a controlled restart sequence and verify normal operation.  
Rationale: reduces risk of latent faults and ensures return to production readiness.

Sign-off
21. Completion sign-off must include signatures and printed names for the following roles:
21.1 Maintenance lead who performed work.  
21.2 Operations supervisor accepting machine back to service.  
21.3 Safety representative verifying LOTO and hazard controls.  
Records retained with the work order and referenced in the maintenance management system per site retention policy.

References
22. Consult ECN-2026-003 for outage authorization details, MM-P1-L1-IH03 for induction heater maintenance specifics and SOP-P1-L1-02 for production stop and material handling procedures.

Revision history
23. Rev C: Current revision.
